page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.large is an entry-tier instance within the compute-optimized ecs.c7 instance family. Built on KVM hypervisor architecture, it features 2 virtual CPUs powered by 1 physical Intel Xeon 8369B processor core running at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance utilizes 4.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Compute resources are provisioned on a dedicated CPU allocation basis with hyperthreading enabled. Hardware instruction sets include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs, while offering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, single-threaded processing demonstrates average performance within the middle tier, including a stress-ng single-core result of 1874.59, a Geekbench single-core score of 1487.0, and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 27.47 GB/sec. However, due to its physical configuration of a single core, multi-core and highly parallel workload metrics fall into lower performance bands. The instance recorded 1926.09 in multi-core stress-ng testing, 1742.0 in multi-core Geekbench, and 2939.36 in PassMark CPU tests, all ranking in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests also showed limited throughput, achieving 14.32 GB/sec for large block uncached reads and 12.85 GB/sec for uncached writes.

The hardware configuration provides a lightweight compute profile for applications that do not require high concurrency or large memory footprints. Database operations scored 976.1 on PassMark, while Redis SET throughput reached 1.91 million operations per second. Static web serving reached 3.33 GB/sec throughput. Qualitative cost efficiency aligns with small computational tasks where dedicated vCPU predictability is required without paying for unneeded RAM or multi-core capacity. Recommended workload fits include low-concurrency web serving, single-threaded batch execution, light microservices, and small utility background tasks.
